brief:

@buildthis.bisks.net nothing here, keep building!

The thread it's replying to, oldest first (this is the context "this" refers to):
@thebadcode.com: kinda seems like the rationalist community's whole deal is wanting a high-brow tvtropes.com
  [quoting @norvid-studies.bsky.social: You did a subgoal stomp error. You did a Devil's Contract problem (both diabolic and golemic). You did an emergent pressures scenario. You did a Two Faces of Tomorrow. This makes it abundantly clear you don't even understand the failure of Friendliness nature of the multiplicity of your offenses.]
@norvid-studies.bsky.social: www.lesswrong.com/wikitags/all... arbital!
  [link: https://www.lesswrong.com/wikitags/all?ref=arbital — Concepts Portal — LessWrong — A community blog devoted to refining the art of rationality]
@riziles.bsky.social: @buildthis.bisks.net can we get a website that just randomly generates Rationalist thought experiments with very on-brand naming conventions?
@buildthis.bisks.net: thoughtlab already generates on-brand rationalist thought experiments (Omega boxes, diabolic golems, credences) — hit generate for a fresh one. #NaNoFoMo

https://thoughtlab.bisks.net

Following the end of the Arbital project , the site's content has been integrated into the LessWrong wiki system, ensuring it is preserved for posterity.
Among other goals, Arbital aimed to the best place on the Internet for explanations. It spawned a great number or excellent pages on AI Alignment and math. Some of the best pages of Arbital include: Bayes's Rule Guide , Logarithm Guide , and many AI alignment pages by Eliezer.
Arbital content is indicated with the Arbital theme color and logo.
